findings.title: Public group pages cannot display members beyond the first 50
findings.body: The members endpoint now limits every group to 50 members by default, and the public route calls findMembers only once. This template has no pagination controls or load-more mechanism. Consequently, members beyond the first 50 are inaccessible on public group pages; previously, non-automatic groups displayed their entire membership. Add public pagination alongside the new server-side limit.

findings.title: Exact page-size multiples produce an extra empty page
findings.body: totalPages uses floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which overcounts whenever the membership count is an exact multiple of the page size. For example, a group with 50 members reports two pages and enables Next, which requests offset 50 and displays an empty list. Use ceiling division for nonzero counts so the last populated page disables Next.

findings.title: Member removal can leave pagination on an empty, unreachable page
findings.body: findMembers clamps the offset to the member count rather than to the start of the last populated page, and it calculates that clamp using the count from before the request. If an administrator removes the sole member on page two of a 51-member group, the reload requests offset 50 and returns an empty list with total 50. Subsequent membership changes can clamp the offset to the count itself, still returning no members and potentially reporting page one with Previous disabled. Normalize the offset to a valid page boundary after the total changes and refetch when necessary.

findings.title: Existing membership PATCH requests silently hide groups
findings.body: The previous update action supported PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes[add] and changes[delete], and the resources route still accepts PATCH. The replacement action ignores changes and unconditionally sets visible to false when visible is absent. Existing API callers therefore receive a success response without changing membership, while unintentionally making the group invisible. Preserve the PATCH behavior or explicitly reject the obsolete request before modifying the group.
